title: PLAN REVIEW PROMPT PACK
sub: Ten checks to run against a drawing set PDF before the first coordination meeting. One master prompt, ten passes.
get: One master prompt that sets role, inputs and output table
Ten named passes you can run one at a time
Works in Claude or ChatGPT with the PDF attached

sections.label: Prompt
sections.text:
You are a senior preconstruction manager reviewing a drawing set for constructability before the first coordination meeting. The attached PDF is the set. Project: {project name}, {type}, {approx. SF}, {delivery method}.

Run PASS {n} below. For every finding return one row: Sheet | Grid/Location | Finding | Why it matters | Suggested RFI or action | Severity (High/Med/Low). Cite the sheet number for every row. If you cannot verify something from the drawings, say so instead of guessing.

PASSES
1 Missing or conflicting dimensions between plan, section and detail
2 Door and window schedule vs. plan tags: count, size, fire rating
3 Structural vs. architectural: openings, slab depressions, beam depths at ceilings
4 MEP routing vs. structure: duct mains through beams, no shaft shown
5 Finish schedule vs. room plan: unlisted rooms, missing floor transitions
6 Accessibility: clearances, turning radii, ramp slopes, reach ranges
7 Exterior envelope: flashing, air barrier continuity, control joints
8 Specified products called out on drawings but absent from the spec index
9 Phasing and site logistics: crane reach, laydown, temp power, egress during construction
10 Long-lead items visible on drawings: switchgear, elevators, curtain wall, custom steel

Finish each pass with the three findings you would raise first and why.

title: CHANGE-ORDER RISK INBOX TRIAGE
sub: Every incoming project email gets read for change-order language and tagged. The ones that cost money rise to the top of the morning.
get: Gmail or Outlook rules plus one assistant classification step
Risk vocabulary list you can extend
Daily digest format

sections.label: Build steps
items: Create a label/category per project and one called CO-RISK.
Rule: any email from a project contact or with the project number in the subject gets the project label.
Automation (Zapier/Make/n8n or Power Automate): on new labeled email, send subject + body to the assistant with the classification prompt.
Assistant returns: risk level (none/low/high), the trigger phrase, and a one-line reason.
High → apply CO-RISK, star it, add to a sheet with date, sender, phrase, and the notice deadline from your contract (e.g. 7 days).
7:00 AM digest email: all CO-RISK items from the last 24 hours, oldest deadline first.

sections.label: Prompt inside the automation
sections.text: Classify this construction project email for change-order or claim risk. Risk phrases include: extra, additional, not in our scope, revised, delay, impact, backcharge, hold, differing condition, unforeseen, direction to proceed, acceleration, time extension, notice. Return JSON: {"risk":"none|low|high","phrase":"…","reason":"one sentence","suggested_action":"reply / log notice / call PM"}. High = money or time is being claimed or directed. Low = language suggests it may come.

title: PROPOSAL SECTION DRAFTER
sub: Five proposal sections drafted from your past proposals, the RFP, and the project list. You review and sharpen, not write.
get: Five section prompts: approach, team, relevant experience, schedule narrative, safety
Source folder structure so the assistant has your voice
Compliance matrix check at the end

sections.label: Prompt
sections.text:
Sources attached: the RFP, our last three winning proposals, the project list, and résumés. Draft Section {n} for {project}:

1 Project approach: restate the owner's stated priorities from the RFP in order, then our approach to each, one paragraph per priority, specific to this site and schedule.
2 Team: org chart text and a 60-word bio per key person, drawn from résumés; pair each person with the RFP's stated evaluation criteria.
3 Relevant experience: pick the five most comparable projects from the list by type, size and owner; 80 words each with value, dates, role, and one measurable outcome.
4 Schedule narrative: milestones from the RFP, our sequencing logic, the two risks and how they are controlled.
5 Safety: EMR, incident rates and the three program elements most relevant to this project's hazards.

Match the tone of our past proposals. No superlatives. Flag every claim that needs a number we have not provided. Finish with a compliance matrix: RFP requirement → section and page where it is answered.
